board: Alabama State Board of Public Accountancy

cycle.note: Alabama CPE years run October 1 – September 30: 40 hours, including 2 ethics and 8 accounting & auditing (30-X-5, amended effective Oct 15, 2026). Annual permits expire September 30; the renewal application and fee are due by December 31.

requirements.label: Annual CPE
requirements.note: 40 hours each fiscal year ending September 30 (30-X-5-.02).

requirements.label: Accounting & auditing
requirements.note: At least 8 of the 40 in accounting and auditing — required of every active CPA.

requirements.label: Personal development
requirements.note: Maximum, not a target. No more than 12 personal development hours count.

requirements.label: Nano-learning
requirements.note: Maximum, not a target. Nano-learning is limited to 25% (10 hours).

requirements.label: Ethics
requirements.note: At least 2 hours in a qualifying ethics course every year.

newLicensee.note: If you went active within 5 years of passing the CPA exam, your first 40 hours are due by the end of the first full CPE year: the September 30 one year after the September 30 following your election (30-X-5-.02(2)). Courses count from October 1.

licenseDateHint: Alabama annual permits expire every September 30. The renewal application and fee are due by December 31. CPE years run October–September.
issueDateHint: If you went active this CPE year (since October 1), your first 40 hours are due by the September 30 after next. Courses count from October 1.
yearEndNote: due September 30; renewal application by December 31
limitsNotTracked: Teaching: twice the lecture hours, no credit for repeats.
Software courses count as A&A only if about accounting or audit applications.
Publications: up to 50% of the requirement (more with Board approval).
Credit is in 50-minute hours; after the first hour, in 1/5 or 1/2 hour steps. Self-study minimum 25 minutes; nano-learning minimum 10 minutes at 1/5 hour.
Going active again, or more than 5 years after the exam: 40 hours for each non-active year (max 120) in the 3 years before, with 20% A&A and 5% ethics.
Non-residents may meet their principal-office state's CPE rules instead, if that state has CPE.
A failed CPE audit means the Board also audits your next two fiscal years.
recordRetention: Keep CPE records for 5 years after completion.
